result:
I've saved the Q3 answers to `answer.json`. Running the same script on Q2 reproduces all 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 308,453,332원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | acc, 301,822,291원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u32@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 238 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 685,248원 |
| h. August → September growth | 0.7% |

To match the Q2 reference values, I had to make three assumptions about the data:

- **Dates are in Korean time (UTC+9).** Order times are stored in UTC, so I shifted them by +9 hours before deciding which quarter and month each order falls in. Using raw UTC dates gave different Q2 results.
- **Segment names are messy.** Values like `Enterprise ` and ` consumer` differ only in case or spaces, so I lowercased and trimmed them before grouping.
- **One customer can have several records.** There are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails, so I counted customers by email for b, e and f. Counting by customer ID gave 275 and 214 for Q2 instead of the reference 234 and 195.

The data has no April orders at all, so Q2 only covers May and June.
